body.statement: For every \(n\), the directed-dyadic bandwidth satisfies \(x_n\le h_n\le x_n+2^{-n}\). Uniformly over the declared class, \(x_n\to0\) and hence \(h_n\to0\). In particular, \(0\le5(h_n-x_n)\le5\cdot2^{-n}\), so dyadic rounding inflates the reported radius \(a_n+5h_n\) by at most \(5\cdot2^{-n}\) relative to \(a_n+5x_n\).
body.justification: The explicit dyadic bracket makes the smoothing choice effective and isolates its finite numerical contribution to interval radius.
body.gap: The nearby adaptive-inference results do not track directed rounding of an atom-safe smoothing bandwidth through an oracle-radius comparison.
body.consumer: The coverage theorem and clinical-log implementation receive an auditable \(5\cdot2^{-n}\) radius charge rather than an unspecified approximation error.
